title: Offline world data for The Mathematics of You
recordSchema: Each observation inherits its unit, source, access date and notes from the containing series unless the observation supplies a more specific source URL or note.
historicalRecordSchema: Historical records retain a numeric value for existing calculation utilities and may add lowerBound/upperBound for a published estimate range, uncertainty for a reported measurement uncertainty, periodStart/periodEnd for a period statistic, and observationType or valueSource so the method remains explicit.

methodology.latestYearRule: Use the last non-null published observation in each series. A documented current-year partial observation may be used only with its exact period label; never relabel an earlier year or a partial period as today or as a completed annual value.
methodology.birthYearRule: Use an official observation for the visitor's birth year when one exists. Do not silently substitute the closest year.
methodology.historicalSeriesRule: Historical census anchors, proxy reconstructions and period estimates are stored as separate named series. Do not silently merge them with modern harmonized series or imply that their methods are identical.
methodology.historicalFallbackRule: When a birth year predates a comparable series, show the first relevant observation or benchmark with its real year and method. Never extrapolate backward or relabel a later observation as the birth-year value.
methodology.rangeRule: When historical sources disagree, preserve the published range and identify any single displayed value by its named source rather than presenting a midpoint as an observation.
methodology.interpolationFormula: estimated value = y0 + ((date - date0) / (date1 - date0)) * (y1 - y0)
methodology.interpolationRule: Interpolate only between adjacent observations when the series explicitly allows it, label the result as interpolated, and name both surrounding years. No extrapolation is allowed.
methodology.purchasingPowerFormula: equivalent rupees in latest data year = rupees in selected starting year * (latest CPI / selected starting CPI)
methodology.marketGrowthFormula: price-index growth (%) = ((latest dated close / first comparable stored close) - 1) * 100

nifty50YearEnd.label: NIFTY 50 price index — dated official closes
nifty50YearEnd.frequency: last available official December close for 2011–2025, plus the 14 August 2026 current-year close

derivedCalculation.name: NIFTY 50 price-index growth
derivedCalculation.formula: growth (%) = ((latest dated close / first comparable stored close) - 1) * 100
derivedCalculation.assumption: This compares dated price-index levels. The 2026 endpoint is a current-year close, not a year-end close. The calculation excludes dividends, fees, taxes and the exact timing of a visitor's birth, so it is not an investment-return calculation.

interpolation.reason: Market prices are not linearly interpolated. Use only the stored official closing observations.

source.title: National Stock Exchange of India — Historical Index Data
source.archivePattern: NSE archives filename pattern: ind_close_all_DDMMYYYY.csv (substitute the requested date)

notes: NIFTY 50 was named S&P CNX Nifty in 2012, CNX Nifty in 2013–2014, and Nifty 50 in later archive files; these observations refer to the same benchmark lineage.
The 2011 point is the 30 December final-trading-day close shown through NSE's official historical-index data service; the later static daily archive pattern was not available for that date.
The 2026 point is the official NIFTY 50 close on 14 August 2026. It is a current-year checkpoint, not a year-end value, and can change substantially before year-end.
Do not describe this price-index change as money earned: it excludes dividends and all investor-specific costs.

values.note: Final trading-day close for calendar year 2011; verified through NSE's official historical-index data service.

values.sourceTitle: National Stock Exchange of India — Indices closing prices, 14 August 2026

genuineLimitations: The modern World Bank-backed series begin in different years: 1960 for population, broad CPI and life expectancy; 1990 for internet use; 1993 for electricity access; and 1981 for the first sparse adult-literacy observation. A value from the first available year must never be relabelled as an earlier visitor's birth-year value.

The four separately named historical series contain census anchors or isolated benchmarks, not seamless annual extensions of the modern series. Their different methods, periods, geography and uncertainty must remain visible.

For a 1900 birth there is no comparable birth-year value for internet use, electricity access, broad Indian CPI, adult literacy aged 15+, or NIFTY 50. Those cards must state when their records begin rather than fabricate or extrapolate a number.
Different series end in different years. The interface must print each series' actual latest period and distinguish current-year checkpoints from complete annual observations.
World Bank values can be revised after this access date. The saved observations intentionally remain frozen so the exhibition continues to work offline and reproducibly.
Adult-literacy observations are irregular and must not be interpolated.
The NIFTY series is a price-index comparison at dated endpoints, not a personalised investment return; its 2026 endpoint is a current-year close rather than a year-end close.
